reasons: Amber: CCC credit spread (OAS), AI basket drawdown / momentum, Breadth (RSP/SPY, % above 50dma)
Regime: credit-led — Credit is involved — more serious than an equity-only dip.
Hedge pricing (not in composite): Put skew / cost of tail insurance moderate, Implied vol richness (VIX pctile, IV−RV) cheap

indicators.label: HY credit spread (OAS)
indicators.detail: Level 2.70% (amber ≥4.5%), 5d change -15bp (amber ≥+30bp). A fast widening is the best short-lead credit signal.

indicators.label: CCC credit spread (OAS)
indicators.detail: Junkiest credit tier — closest public proxy for the leveraged AI periphery.

indicators.label: HYG/IEF ratio (credit vs safety)
indicators.detail: High-yield ETF vs Treasuries — a same-day credit read with no FRED lag.

indicators.label: Leveraged loans (BKLN)
indicators.detail: Floating-rate senior secured loans — isolates credit risk from rate moves. Tracking HY closely (-0.1pp 10d).

indicators.label: SOFR − IORB (funding stress)
indicators.detail: Repo rate over the interest-on-reserves floor; a persistent positive spread means funding stress.

indicators.label: Funding tail (SOFR spread + Fed repo use)
indicators.detail: SOFR 99th−1st percentile 13bp (amber ≥30bp); Fed repo ops $0.0bn (3d max) (amber ≥$5bn). Needs both legs to confirm stress over calendar effects.

indicators.label: Chicago Fed NFCI
indicators.detail: Weekly financial-conditions composite; positive = tighter than average.

indicators.label: VIX term structure (VIX/VIX3M)
indicators.detail: ≥1.00 = backwardation — the near-coincident confirmation signal (days of lead at most).

indicators.label: Put skew / cost of tail insurance
indicators.detail: SKEW 137 (expensive ≥145), VVIX 93 (expensive ≥110). Tail insurance is moderately priced. Cost tier, not a risk tier — excluded from the composite.

indicators.label: Implied vol richness (VIX pctile, IV−RV)
indicators.detail: VIX 15.5 sits at the 17th percentile of its trailing year (expensive ≥80th); 20d realized 14.0, so implied carries +1.5 vol points of premium (expensive ≥8). Cost tier, not a risk tier — excluded from the composite.

indicators.label: Periphery canaries (CRWV, ORCL)
indicators.detail: Sharp equity drops or realized-vol spikes in the debt-financed periphery stand in for CDS.

indicators.label: Breadth (RSP/SPY, % above 50dma)
indicators.detail: Narrowing breadth = fragility backdrop; slow signal, low weight.

indicators.label: Yield curve (10y−3m)
indicators.detail: Inversion is a 6–18 month gauge, not a timing signal — capped at amber.

items.headline: Banks hit concentration limits on data-center debt, pushing exposure to pension funds and insurers
items.note: Banks are hitting exposure caps to the same handful of hyperscale tenants, forcing more AI data-center debt into the less-regulated 144A/private-credit channel held by pensions and insurers.

items.headline: SEC exempts data-center bonds from key asset-backed-securities rules, easing debt issuance
items.note: Removing risk-retention and disclosure requirements for a class of data-center securitizations lowers the bar for issuance just as the sector's debt load is drawing credit scrutiny.

items.headline: Oracle-led hyperscaler CDS spreads hit fresh records; Oracle's 5-year CDS at 215bp, up 70bp YTD
items.note: Oracle's CDS spread widened past the 2008-crisis peak with Meta and Broadcom also hitting record levels, a broad-based credit-market signal of rising AI financing risk beyond a single name.

items.headline: AI debt indigestion forces Wall Street to rethink bond sales as ~80% of data-center securities trade wider than issuance
items.note: Broad-based secondary-market spread widening across data-center debt sold since early 2025 signals waning investor appetite after the year's fundraising surge.

items.headline: CMBS investors push back on AI-linked data-center debt; CyrusOne and QTS deals had to widen pricing to clear
items.note: Two of the last three data-center-backed commercial mortgage bonds needed repricing to attract buyers, a concrete sign of spread widening spreading into the CMBS corner of AI credit.

items.headline: SoftBank's AI funding plans face reckoning: $30B of obligations due in H2 2026 plus a $40B bridge loan maturing March 2027
items.note: Lenders are wary of using SoftBank's OpenAI stake as loan collateral, and its margin-loan LTV against Arm shares is running well above SoftBank's own reported ratio, tightening the path to fund its AI commitments.
